subject: Clarifying backup RPO/RTO and deletion propagation for FinTrust datasets
messages:
From: Alice Martin <alice.martin@fintrust.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@fintrust.com
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Backup retention & deletion behavior (data residency)

Hi Karthik —

Quick Q ahead of our security review next week: for FinTrust data that lives in the us-east region under our contract, can you confirm: 

1) How long backups (snapshots) are retained by default and whether retention is tied to the primary data retention policy or managed separately.
2) If a customer requests immediate deletion of an account and primary data is purged, how and when do backups (including cross-region DR snapshots) get removed?
3) Are there manual steps that require Redwood ops involvement, or is deletion fully automated through the control plane (with audit logs)?

We also need an RPO/RTO statement for our DR plan and a simple diagram of deletion propagation for auditors.

Thanks — appreciate a concise summary and any links to docs we can attach to our SOC review.

Best,
Alice Martin
Head of Cloud Security | FinTrust Bank

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Martin <alice.martin@fintrust.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Backup retention & deletion behavior (data residency)

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (Product/Security) and Grace (Infrastructure) to provide the precise RPO/RTO numbers and the deletion propagation flow. I can offer a short summary now, and Marissa/Grace will follow with specifics and the diagram.

High-level answers:
- Backups are retained according to a customer-configurable policy; default is 30 days for snapshots and 365 days for periodic cold backups (subject to contract).
- Deletion of primary data starts a controlled workflow that triggers backup expiration flags; live snapshots tied to the dataset are marked for deletion and removed according to retention/holding periods unless a legal hold is present.
- For Dedicated/Private deployments there are options to require an ops ticket for manual wipe; hosted customers can opt into auto-delete with audit logs.

I'll let Marissa provide the formal RPO/RTO numbers and attach a simple deletion propagation diagram.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Martin <alice.martin@fintrust.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Backup retention & deletion behavior (data residency)

Alice —

Thanks for looping us in. Below is a short formal answer you can include in your audit materials, plus two attachments: a one-page RPO/RTO summary and a deletion propagation diagram.

Executive summary (for auditors):
- Default snapshot retention (hosted): 30 days
- Default cold backup retention (hosted archive): 365 days (customer-configurable to shorter/longer within contract limits and region constraints)
- RTO (recovery time objective): 15 minutes for warm pool restores (typical small-state datasets), up to 2 hours for full instance restores depending on size and region
- RPO (recovery point objective): continuous KV-cache/append-only log for streaming requests (sub-second for in-flight), snapshot-based RPO of up to 1 hour for scheduled snapshots; customers can enable more aggressive snapshot cadence for tighter RPOs

Deletion propagation behavior:
- When a customer requests deletion via the control plane (or via API), the platform initiates a three-stage workflow: 1) immediate soft-delete flagging on primary objects, 2) cascade to dependent services (KV cache, indexes) and mark associated snapshots with "pending deletion" metadata, 3) final purge according to retention windows or immediate purge if customer selected "immediate wipe" and has the correct contract/BAA in place.
- Cross-region DR snapshots are only purged after verifying no active retention holds; for customers with cross-region replication enabled, replication is disabled immediately on deletion request and the DR snapshots enter the same pending-deletion lifecycle.
- Audit logs capture each stage (flag set, replication disabled, snapshot deletion timestamp) and are exportable to your SIEM via our log-forwarding integration.

Exceptions / manual ops involvement:
- Hosted API customers: deletion can be fully automated if the contract permits; in that case an automated job finalizes snapshot purge within 24 hours of the retention window expiring.
- Dedicated/Private deployments: customers can require an ops ticket for physical media or HSM key destruction; we document and sign-off on completion.
- Legal/regulatory holds: any legal hold will prevent snapshot purge until lifted; holds are visible in the control plane and in exported audit logs.

Attachments included:
- redwood_backup_rpo_rto_summary_v1.pdf (one-page RPO/RTO table + bullet notes)
- snapshot-deletion-flow-diagram.png (sequence diagram showing the three-stage lifecycle)

If you want, I can add an explicit sample audit statement (signed) for your package.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Security Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Alice Martin <alice.martin@fintrust.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Backup retention & deletion behavior (data residency)

Adding a couple of infra-specific notes to Marissa's response:

- Technical detail: snapshots are implemented as immutable object-store manifests + delta layers. When a deletion is requested we mark manifests as expirable and schedule object-level deletes; this avoids accidental breaks for in-flight restorations.
- Cross-region replication: we maintain a replication manifest. On deletion, we disable the replication job immediately and write an audit event. The replicated objects themselves are queued for deletion subject to retention policy.
- Keys: if a customer requests cryptographic key destruction, we can coordinate KMS/HSM key rotation/destruction; for on-prem HSMs we require a jointly-scheduled ceremony.
- Timeline example: customer requests deletion Feb 1; primary dataset soft-deleted immediately, snapshots marked pending deletion Feb 1; if default retention = 30d, final purge job runs Mar 3 (approx) unless immediate-wipe chosen.

Grace
Director, Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
